description: Snapshot authorization (SPEC §7.1) in wire version 2: ../basis.json's cases over a chain with composite keys, with tails of at most four entries. A commit binds, per identity, a chain entry (`seq`, `hash` of the signed entry, `rec`: the seq of the newest recovery-signed entry at or before it, absent if none) with a `tail` of signed entries ending at it. A committer carries the entries back to, but not including, the newest recovery-signed entry, at most the newest four; a member accepts any tail of one to four. A member joins the tail to its own `copy` of the chain (or can't), validates the whole, checks it against the group's `floor` for the identity, and makes one check on the bound state: `device` (the key is a device: an added leaf, an approval signer, the committer) or `not-device` (a Remove by a member who isn't an admin). `key_hex` is the device key, the Ed25519 component of its composite key. Entries are JCS `signed` text, genesis first.

keys.recovery: recovery keys 1 and 2 from v2/recovery.json (genesis commits to key 1)

notice: Test vectors for Tieroute wire version 2 (SPEC version 2.0, draft). These keys are public: never use them for anything real.
rules: The tail has 1 to 4 entries with consecutive seq, each one's prev the hash of the one before, the last one's hash equal to `hash` and its seq to `seq`. Otherwise: invalid.

If the tail starts after genesis, the member needs entries 0 to tail[0].seq - 1 whose last hashes to tail[0].prev. If its copy (or anything it can fetch) has them: joined. If its copy has a different entry at that seq: pending (conflicting histories). If it has nothing that far: pending.
The joined chain must validate (SPEC §6.4 rules 1 to 4, ts non-decreasing; no clock or vouching checks), belong to `identity_id`, and have `rec` right. Otherwise: invalid.

With a floor: the joined chain contains it (the entry at floor.seq hashes to floor.hash), or its newest recovery-signed entry has a seq greater than floor.rec (or there's one, and floor.rec is absent). Otherwise: invalid.
`device`: the key is a device after the last entry. `not-device`: it isn't, and without a floor it must have been a device somewhere in the chain. Otherwise: invalid.
